record.original_question: Prove that for every generalized minimal flow u(x,t), the vorticity level sets curl u(x,t)=const are real-analytic curves.

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Prove that for any GM-flow u(x, t) the level lines of vorticity curl u(x, t) = const are real-analytic. One other property of GM-flows is observed in the numerical simulations, cf. Figure 3. The flow domain M contains some number of vorticity blobs B1 , . . . , BN and a background B0 . Accurate numerical results hint at the following conjecture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a domain M ⊂ ℝ² (or a two-dimensional Riemannian manifold), governing a velocity field u(x,t) that is divergence-free and satisfies
  ∂_t u + (u · ∇) u + ∇p = 0,  div u = 0.
A generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) is a weak solution u(x,t) of these equations obtained as a limit of approximate minimizers of the action functional
  A[u] = ½ ∫₀^T ∫_M |u(x,t)|² dx dt
on the space of incompressible flows realizing a prescribed pair of initial and final configurations (i.e. of measure-preserving transformations of M), in the sense of generalized incompressible flows minimizing kinetic energy between two volume-preserving diffeomorphisms.

Let ω(x,t) = curl u(x,t) denote the scalar vorticity associated with such a GM-flow u.

Prove that for every GM-flow u(x,t), and every regular value c of ω(·,t), the vorticity level set
  { x ∈ M : curl u(x,t) = c }
is a union of real-analytic curves in M, for every fixed time t in the interval of definition.
artifact.category_tag: Generalized Euler flows and vorticity regularity
artifact.status_search_result: The problem concerns analytic regularity of vorticity level sets for generalized minimal (action-minimizing) flows in the sense of Brenier–Shnirelman. Searches surface foundational work on generalized fluid flows and recent results on maximally mixed equilibria, but no result establishing the real-analyticity of vorticity level lines for arbitrary GM-flows was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Generalized fluid flows, their approximation and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Shnirelman's framework of generalized incompressible flows minimizing kinetic energy between volume-preserving diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the GM-flow framework but does not address analyticity of vorticity level lines.

status_evidence.title: On Maximally Mixed Equilibria of Two-Dimensional Perfect Fluids
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on equilibria of 2D perfect fluids related to mixing and minimization.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not resolve analyticity of vorticity level sets for GM-flows.

status_evidence.title: Publications of Alexander Shnirelman
status_evidence.snippet: List of Shnirelman's publications on generalized flows and Euler equations.
status_evidence.claim: No listed work resolves the real-analytic level-line problem for GM-flows.
